objective.name: remote_health.py
objective.purpose: Health check for the remotely-hosted Expo Go staging server. Fetches the QR-code page from https://bubble-mobile.replit.app/qr-code, validates the HTML contains an exp:// URL, and (optionally) opens that URL in an iOS simulator, Android emulator, Genymotion device, or browser. Caches ETag/timestamp in ~/.remote_health_state.json to detect unchanged builds (HTTP 304). No-arg behavior: fetch the remote page and print whether the build is new (200) or unchanged (304).
objective.side_effects: HTTP GETs to bubble-mobile.replit.app and the GitHub API. Writes ~/.remote_health_state.json. May download/cache Expo Go assets in ~/.expo_go_cache and install/uninstall the Expo Go app on a sim/emulator. Opens URLs in a sim/emulator/browser.
objective.language_packages: stdlib only (argparse, hashlib, json, re, socket, subprocess, shutil, tarfile, tempfile, urllib, webbrowser, datetime, pathlib)
path_assumptions: runs from any cwd; state lives in $HOME
host_requirements: Network reachability to bubble-mobile.replit.app and api.github.com
macOS for osascript window-foreground and xcrun (iOS)
A booted iOS sim / Android emulator / Genymotion device only when an --ios/--android/--genymotion open is requested

switches.effect: Open the exp:// URL in a booted iOS simulator (xcrun; auto-installs Expo Go if missing)
Open in a running Android emulator (adb; auto-installs Expo Go)
Open in a Genymotion device (gmtool + adb)
Open in the default browser (exp:// → https://)
Uninstall Expo Go first, forcing a fresh install
Pin the Expo Go release to a matching SDK version when installing
Fetch exp:// from the remote staging server (default; mutually exclusive with --local/--exp_url)
Use the supplied exp:// URL directly

objective.explicit_env_checks: false — no env-var checks; URLs are hard-coded constants. Validates HTTP status, Content-Type, exp:// presence, and device availability before opening

subjective.usual_invocation: Run manually by a developer to confirm the Replit-hosted Expo Go build is live and to push it onto a sim/emulator for a quick look. Note: per project memory, Expo Go is effectively broken for SDK 55, so this tool's open-in-Expo-Go path is of limited current use.
subjective.invocation_change_recommendation: Switch form is already used and fine. Lower-priority: the interactive multi-device numbered prompt could gain a --device flag so it can run non-interactively in scripts.
subjective.linux_changes_needed: Core health check (fetch + 304 detection) is fully portable. macOS-specific bits to guard for Linux: osascript window-foreground (drop / make best-effort no-op) and xcrun/iOS (skip; Linux has no iOS sim). Android (adb) and browser (webbrowser) paths work on Linux. So: portable for --remote/--local/--web; --ios unavailable on Linux.

macos_dependency.notes: True for full feature set (osascript foreground, xcrun iOS open). False for the core remote/local/web health check, which is stdlib-portable.

subjective.typical_runtime: A few seconds for a plain fetch (10s page timeout, 15s GitHub API timeout, warns if >4s). Longer only when it downloads/installs Expo Go assets (network-bound, one-time per tag).
subjective.slow_switch_warning: No switch reliably exceeds 2 minutes; -r/--reinstall plus a cold Expo Go download is the slowest path but is network-bound, not inherently long.
subjective.dry_run_recommendation: Yes — a --dry-run that performs the fetch/validation and reports what it WOULD install/open, without uninstalling/installing apps or launching anything. The install/uninstall steps are the ones worth previewing.
subjective.destructive_steps: Uninstalls the Expo Go app (xcrun simctl uninstall / adb uninstall) on -r/--reinstall, and installs APK/IPA assets. These mutate device state but not project files. The failure-path message suggests deleting ~/.remote_health_state.json.
subjective.rewrite_language_recommendation: No. Python stdlib HTTP + subprocess is appropriate.
subjective.merge_recommendation: Keep standalone for now. Given Expo Go SDK-55 breakage, candidate for deprecation rather than merging; revisit when Expo Go support returns.
subjective.rename_recommendation: Optional — name is accurate. Could drop .py if standardizing command names.
subjective.relocate_recommendation: Defensible to move to a scripts/dev/ or scripts/expo/ area since it serves the (currently broken) Expo Go path and is used less than the core runners.
subjective.improvement_suggestions: Lift the hard-coded URLs (TARGET_URL, GitHub releases API, Replit login) into env vars or config/environments.json so non-default deployments are testable. Add a --device selector to avoid the interactive prompt in automation. Add a --dry-run. Consider a non-zero exit on 'build unchanged when change expected' for CI gating.
subjective.requirements_check_completeness: explicit and incomplete — checks HTTP status/Content-Type/exp:// presence and device existence, but network failure handling is narrow (gaierror/URLError) and there are no env-var or tool-presence preflights.
subjective.external_dependency_breakdown: Scoring policy (v1.0): +1 per env var; +1 per non-standard / separately-installed program (xcrun/simctl, Android SDK tools, maestro, grpcurl, psql, gmtool, node/npm, lnav, etc.); programs shipped with macOS (ps, lsof, top, pgrep, sysctl, open, pbcopy, curl, osascript, system_profiler, git, grep/sed/awk) are NOT counted; +5 if a simulator/emulator is required on the primary path; +10 per large non-default app required (Xcode, Android Studio/SDK, Genymotion, Postgres, brew). Here: env 0 (URLs hard-coded, not env) + programs 3 (xcrun, adb, gmtool) + sim 0 + apps 0 = 3. (osascript ships with macOS, not counted.) A --ios/--android open adds an effective +5 sim and +10 app on that path.
subjective.change_score_rationale: Weights (v1.0): Linux portability full-block +8 / partial +4 / portable 0; other dimensions +1 (or +2 where noted). Linux partial +4 (iOS/osascript blocked; core+android+web portable). Invocation (add --device for non-interactive) +1. Missing --dry-run +1. Destructive app uninstall/install +1. Gating incomplete +1. Hard-coded-URLs improvement +1. Total 9.
subjective.quality_score_rationale: Anchored rubric (v1.0), sub-scores sum to 100 — Error-handling/robustness /25: 18; Tests /20: 0 (no self-tests); Structure/clarity /20: 15; Documentation /15: 10; Portability + explicit requirement checks /20: 11. Total 54. Good ETag/SHA256 caching and redirect tracking; docked for hard-coded URLs, narrow network error handling, a blocking interactive device prompt, and no tests. Serves a currently-broken Expo Go path.
